newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan king in solidarity trip to PLO-ruled Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Jordan king in solidarity trip to PLO-ruled Gaza.

text.p: King Hussein of Jordan arrived on his first visit to the PLO-ruled Gaza Strip on Sunday to show solidarity with the Palestinians while their peace talks with Israel falter, witnesses said.

The king arrived as the PLO warned that U.S.-brokered peace talks with Israel to launch self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron were near a dead end. U.S. envoy Dennis Ross was due to leave the region on Sunday after failing to clinch a deal in a three-week shuttle.
Witnesses said the Jordanian monarch stepped onto a red carpet from his helicopter beneath clear Gazan skies. The king was greeted by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
The two men stood on a stage bedecked with Jordanian and Palestinian flags and inspected a military honour guard.
"This is a great honour and encouragement from him to push the peace process forward and to strengthen the Palestinian-Jordanian relationship," Arafat told Israel Radio earlier on Sunday.
King Hussein and Arafat have a history of uneasy relations, but Arab frustration with Netanyahu appears to have brought them closer together.

The monarch became the first Arab head of state to visit the Palestinian self-ruled areas when he met Arafat in the West Bank enclave of Jericho last October. It was his first visit to the West Bank since Israel seized it from Jordan in a 1967 war.

The king landed at Arafat's office in Gaza City after Israel refused a Palestinian request to receive the monarch's helicopter at an airport in the south of the strip. Israel demands security control of the airport.
The trip came on the heels of protests last week against an Israeli trade fair in Amman, the largest anti-Israeli demonstrations since Jordan signed a peace treaty with the Jewish state in 1994.
The king was accompanied by Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti. The leaders went into Arafat's office for talks.
Arafat and King Hussein are expected to have Iftar together, the meal at dusk that Moslems take after fasting during daylight hours in the holy month of Ramadan.
Palestinians, who fled to Jordan after Israel's creation in 1948 and the following Arab-Israeli wars, are widely thought to form a majority of Jordan's population.
"If you drop a stone in the West Bank, we feel the ripples in Jordan," a senior Jordanian official said recently.
